description: Generated from the scrim settings registry by `scrim config schema`. Do not edit.

token.description: Reference to the bearer token operators present on a TCP admin listener (admin.url http://host:port). Required for TCP; the Unix socket uses peer credentials instead. scrim approve and friends send it.

url.description: Address of the scrim admin API for operator commands: unix:/path/to/socket or http(s)://host:port. Empty means unix:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/scrim/admin.sock.

group.description: Group (name or ID) the API socket belongs to, so members can connect with api.permissions 0660. scrim must be a member. Empty keeps the group of the process.

permissions.description: Permission bits of the API socket, octal. Widen (for example 0660) only to let agents running as other local users connect; their identity still comes from peer credentials.

socket.description: Unix socket of the local agent API. Empty uses $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/scrim/api.sock.

listen.description: TCP address that serves only the decision-link endpoint, for approvals.public-url to point at (usually through a TLS reverse proxy). Empty means decision links are served on the admin listener only.

poll-interval.description: How often a waiting operation re-reads its approval from the state backend; bounds how long a decision recorded on another replica takes to release it when no event announces it (events.backend).

public-url.description: Base URL under which the decision endpoint is reachable from approvers' devices, for example https://scrim.example.org. Empty means notifiers get no decision links and approvals are decided with scrim approve.

signing-key.description: Reference to the key (at least 32 bytes) that signs decision links, shared by every replica. Empty means a random key per process: links stop working on restart and on other replicas.

timeout.description: How long an approval waits for a decision before it is denied. A rule's approval.timeout overrides it.

batch-size.description: How many audit entries one write to the kafka sink carries at most.

brokers.description: Seed brokers (host:port) of the Kafka (or Redpanda) cluster of the kafka audit sink.

password.description: Reference to the SASL password of the kafka audit sink.

policy.description: What happens when the kafka sink's queue is full because the sink is slow or down: block makes the audited operation wait up to audit.kafka.timeout and then refuses it; drop lets it through and counts the entry in scrim_audit_sink_dropped_total (it stays in the database audit log). Never silent either way.

queue-size.description: How many audit entries wait for the kafka sink at most.

sasl-mechanism.description: SASL mechanism of the kafka audit sink; plain needs audit.kafka.tls.

timeout.description: With audit.kafka.policy block, how long an audited operation waits for room in the kafka queue before it is refused.

tls.description: Connect to the Kafka brokers over TLS, verified against the system roots or audit.kafka.tls-ca-file.

tls-ca-file.description: PEM file of the certificate authorities that sign the Kafka broker certificates; empty uses the system roots.

topic.description: Topic the kafka audit sink produces to. Records are keyed by agent, so one agent's entries stay in order on one partition.

username.description: SASL user of the kafka audit sink.

write-timeout.description: How long one write to the kafka sink may take before it counts as failed and is retried.

batch-size.description: How many audit entries one write to the loki sink carries at most.

labels.description: Extra static stream labels for audit entries in Loki, added to service_name=scrim and source=audit. Keep them low-cardinality; per-entry fields are in the JSON line.

password.description: Reference to the basic auth password (or bearer token with an empty audit.loki.username) of the loki audit sink.

policy.description: What happens when the loki sink's queue is full because the sink is slow or down: block makes the audited operation wait up to audit.loki.timeout and then refuses it; drop lets it through and counts the entry in scrim_audit_sink_dropped_total (it stays in the database audit log). Never silent either way.

queue-size.description: How many audit entries wait for the loki sink at most.

tenant.description: Loki tenant (X-Scope-OrgID) for the loki audit sink; empty for a single-tenant Loki.

timeout.description: With audit.loki.policy block, how long an audited operation waits for room in the loki queue before it is refused.

url.description: Base URL of Loki (or a compatible push endpoint) for the loki audit sink; entries are pushed to <url>/loki/api/v1/push.

username.description: Basic auth user for the loki audit sink; empty for none.

write-timeout.description: How long one write to the loki sink may take before it counts as failed and is retried.

batch-size.description: How many audit entries one write to the otlp sink carries at most.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint of the otlp audit sink, a collector or a backend that takes OTLP logs: http(s)://host:4318 (the /v1/logs path is added unless the URL has a path).

policy.description: What happens when the otlp sink's queue is full because the sink is slow or down: block makes the audited operation wait up to audit.otlp.timeout and then refuses it; drop lets it through and counts the entry in scrim_audit_sink_dropped_total (it stays in the database audit log). Never silent either way.

queue-size.description: How many audit entries wait for the otlp sink at most.

timeout.description: With audit.otlp.policy block, how long an audited operation waits for room in the otlp queue before it is refused.

token.description: Reference to a bearer token sent to the otlp audit sink; empty for none.

write-timeout.description: How long one write to the otlp sink may take before it counts as failed and is retried.

sinks.description: Where audit entries go: db (the state backend's audit log, always written, in the transaction of the change it records) plus any of otlp, loki and kafka, each fed from its own bounded queue with the backpressure policy audit.<sink>.policy.

entries.description: Catalog entries by logical name: ref, profiles, variants, prefix, template, hosts, placeholder, class, inject, tools, placeholder_format, aws_sigv4, client_certificate, ssh_key, ssh_certificate. References only, never values.

environment.description: Catalog environment that selects per-environment references.

files.description: Catalog files to load, in order. Each is a YAML document with `kind: Catalog` and an `entries` map. Reloaded when they change.

metadata-from.description: Store prefixes (for example bao://kv/agents) whose secrets' metadata labels are read as catalog entries.

metadata-prefix.description: Prefix of the store metadata keys read as catalog bindings: <prefix>hosts, <prefix>placeholder, <prefix>profiles, <prefix>name, <prefix>class, <prefix>field.

profile.description: Catalog profile (for example dev or prod) that selects per-profile references.

reload-interval.description: How often catalog files are checked for changes.

strict.description: Reject config files containing keys scrim does not know. When false, unknown keys are reported as warnings instead.

watch.description: Reload the configuration when a config file or an included file changes. SIGHUP always triggers a reload.

databases.description: Databases the auth proxies and the read-only database tool reach, by name: `kind` (postgres or mysql), `address` (host:port of the server), `user` and `password` (a reference) scrim logs in with, optional `database` (the only database the agent gets; default the one its client asks for), `listen` (unix:/path or host:port; default a Unix socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/scrim/db/<name>), `listen-permissions` (octal, default 0600), `tls` (verify-full, the default, or insecure-plaintext, which weakens the protection of the session and the server's identity), `tls-ca` (PEM file; default the system roots), `tls-server-name`, `connect-timeout`, `tool` (false turns the read-only database tool off for this database), `query-timeout` (default 10s) and `query-max-rows` (default 1000).

memory-lock.description: Lock the data plane's memory so values are never swapped: auto locks when the memlock limit is unlimited and warns otherwise; require refuses to start without it.

path.description: Path of a scrim-dataplane binary to run instead of the embedded one. For development builds; release builds embed it.

push-debounce.description: How long the control plane waits after a store, catalog, configuration or policy change before it pushes a new snapshot, so bursts of changes become one push.

restart-max-backoff.description: Longest wait between data plane restarts after repeated crashes.

start-timeout.description: How long the data plane may take to start and answer the handshake.

upstream-ca-file.description: PEM bundle of extra root certificates the data plane trusts for upstream TLS, in the LLM proxy and the tool proxy (private API hosts, a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy). The system roots stay trusted. A file that is set but unreadable, or holds no certificate, stops the data plane from starting. Empty means the system roots only.

replicas.description: How many control plane replicas share this configuration and state. More than 1 needs a shared state backend (state.backend postgres) and a shared events backend (events.backend postgres, valkey or nats); start-up fails otherwise.

listen.description: Address of the edge listener the forwarders in agent pods connect to (TLS; callers present a Kubernetes service account token). Empty turns it off. Needs identity.kubernetes.enabled and edge.server-names.

server-names.description: Host names and IP addresses the edge listener's certificate carries, signed by scrim's CA, which forwarders already trust. Required with edge.listen.

api-socket.description: Unix socket the forwarder serves the agent API on, the exec broker included (point SCRIM_API_SOCKET at it). Empty serves none.

ca-file.description: PEM file of the CA the central scrim's certificate must chain to: scrim's CA. No system roots are used.

central.description: host:port of the central scrim's edge listener (edge.listen).

connect-timeout.description: How long the forwarder waits for the central scrim before it refuses the local connection.

databases.description: Databases to forward: the central scrim's database name to a loopback address in the pod (app: 127.0.0.1:5432).

server-name.description: Name the central scrim's certificate is verified for. Empty takes the host of edge-forwarder.central.

socket-permissions.description: Permission bits of the forwarder's Unix sockets, octal. The default lets the agent's containers, which run as other users, connect; the sockets live in a volume only this pod mounts.

ssh-agent-socket.description: Unix socket the forwarder serves the ssh-agent on (point SSH_AUTH_SOCK at it). Empty serves none.

token-file.description: Projected service account token for scrim's audience, read again for every connection and sent to the central scrim only.

listen.description: Loopback address of the page where a human enters a value for secret_ask_human. Port 0 picks a free port.

backend.description: How replicas learn about state changes made elsewhere (approval decisions, grant and session changes, break-glass, configuration reloads). local reads the outbox every events.poll-interval and serves one process; postgres adds LISTEN/NOTIFY on the state database (needs state.backend postgres); valkey and nats publish a wake-up on a Valkey channel (valkey.*) or a NATS subject (nats.*). Every backend delivers from the outbox, so a lost wake-up costs latency, never an event. One of postgres, valkey or nats is required when deployment.replicas is more than 1.

subject.description: NATS subject the nats events backend publishes and subscribes to. Replicas of one deployment share it; two deployments on one NATS account need different subjects.

poll-interval.description: How often the outbox is read when nothing announces new events: always with events.backend local, and while the postgres listener or the valkey or nats subscription is disconnected. It bounds how long a change made on another replica takes to arrive then.

channel.description: Valkey channel the valkey events backend publishes and subscribes to. Replicas of one deployment share it; two deployments on one Valkey need different channels.

allow-same-user.description: Run brokered commands even when they would run as the calling agent's own user. That user can read the command's environment and memory (/proc/<pid>/environ, ptrace), so the agent can read the injected secret. For single-user development only.

commands.description: Commands the exec broker may run with secrets, by the name agents call them: `path` (absolute, required), `secrets` (globs over store references or catalog names whose values the command may receive; its allow list), `inject` (where placeholders are replaced: env, args, stdin; default env), `env-names` (globs of variables the agent may set), `env` (fixed variables, not secret), `dirs` (globs of working directories the agent may choose; default none, a fresh empty directory), `args` (regular expressions; the shell-quoted argument list must match one in full) and `timeout`.

max-output.description: Largest standard output or standard error, in bytes, a brokered command may return. A stream above it is withheld entirely, never cut, because a cut could split a secret past redaction.

path.description: PATH of brokered commands, and the directories a command that is not in exec.commands is looked up in. The agent's PATH is never used.

timeout.description: Longest a brokered command may run; a call can ask for less. The process group is killed when it runs out.

user.description: User name or numeric ID brokered commands run as, with that user's primary group and no supplementary groups. Empty runs them as scrim's own user. scrim needs the right to switch users (root or CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID) when it is set. A command never runs as root or as the calling agent's user.

default-ttl.description: Grant duration when neither the rule nor the approver chooses one.

max-ttl.description: Longest grant any rule or approver can create. A rule's grant.max_ttl can only lower it.

agents.description: Agents by service account: agent name to space-separated selectors sa:NAMESPACE/NAME (globs allowed), scope:SCOPE, label:K=V. A service account no rule maps is the agent NAMESPACE/NAME, or unknown with identity.kubernetes.unmapped: unknown.

api-server.description: Base URL of the Kubernetes API server for TokenReview. Empty uses the in-cluster address (KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST and KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT).

audience.description: Audience an agent's projected service account token must carry. Tokens for any other audience, such as a pod's default API token, are refused.

ca-file.description: CA bundle that verifies the API server.

cache-ttl.description: How long a verified token is trusted before the cluster is asked again, capped at the token's expiry. A deleted pod or service account is refused within this bound.

enabled.description: Identify in-cluster callers by projected service account tokens, verified with the TokenReview API. Pods send the token as the password of the proxy user k8s or as the value of x-scrim-session. On in the k8s profile.

token-file.description: scrim's own service account token, which authorises TokenReview calls (RBAC: create tokenreviews, for example by binding system:auth-delegator). Re-read on every call, since the kubelet rotates it.

unmapped.description: What a verified service account no identity.kubernetes.agents rule maps becomes: derive names the agent NAMESPACE/NAME, unknown treats it as an unknown caller.

peers.description: Agents by local user or group: agent name to space-separated selectors uid:N, user:NAME, gid:N, group:NAME, scope:SCOPE, label:K=V. Empty maps the user scrim runs as to one agent named after it.

store-credentials.description: Static per-agent store credentials: `<store>/<agent>` to a reference (env:, file:, cred: or a store reference) of a store token held for that agent. The fallback for agents without Kubernetes passthrough; a store listed here refuses agents that have none.

store-login.description: Per-agent store login, by store instance: `kubernetes role:<template> [mount:<path>]` logs in to the store (OpenBao Kubernetes auth) with the calling pod's own service account token at the role the template names; {namespace}, {service_account} and {agent} are replaced. A store listed here refuses agents that have no usable identity of their own.

include.description: Files, globs or directories merged after this file, relative to it.

cgroups.description: Control groups (cgroup v2 paths below /sys/fs/cgroup, such as agents.slice) the eBPF transparent mode covers (Linux): `sudo scrim ebpf attach` redirects their TCP connections to ports 80 and 443 to the transparent listener and denies their direct and QUIC egress. Status and doctor report each one that is not attached. Empty: the mode is off.

port.description: Port of the transparent listener on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 that the eBPF transparent mode redirects to. It must match the port of proxy.transparent-listen; nothing listening there means covered connections fail, never go direct. Unset, status and `scrim ebpf attach` use the port of the boot unit `scrim install --ebpf` installed, if any.

format.description: Log record format: text (logfmt) or json, one object per line.

allow-unauthenticated-remote.description: Serve metrics.path on a non-loopback metrics.listen without metrics.auth.token, for a network policy or mesh that already restricts who connects. Anyone who can reach the port reads the metrics.

token.description: Reference to a bearer token (at least 16 bytes) a scraper must present on metrics.path. Required when metrics.listen is not a loopback address, unless metrics.allow-unauthenticated-remote is set. The health endpoints never need it.

enabled.description: Serve Prometheus metrics (control plane and data plane) at metrics.path on metrics.listen. Off: nothing is measured on the request path and no metrics listener is bound.

listen.description: Address of the metrics and health endpoint (/healthz or /livez, /readyz, and metrics.path while metrics.enabled). Used when metrics.enabled is true; set explicitly with metrics.enabled false it serves the health endpoints only. Bind to loopback unless scraped remotely.

path.description: Path of the Prometheus endpoint on metrics.listen.

credentials-file.description: Path to a NATS credentials file (JWT and NKey seed), for decentralised authentication; empty for none.

password.description: Reference to the password of nats.username.

servers.description: NATS server URLs (nats://host:4222, tls://host:4222) used by events.backend nats.

timeout.description: Dial timeout, and the bound on the round trip that confirms a subscription after each reconnect. The client also pings the server at this interval and treats two missed answers as a lost connection.

tls-ca-file.description: PEM file of the certificate authorities that sign the NATS server certificate; empty uses the system roots.

token.description: Reference to a NATS authentication token; empty for none.

username.description: NATS user for user and password authentication; empty for none.

token.description: Reference to an ntfy access token for publishing. Empty publishes anonymously.

topic.description: ntfy topic approval requests are published to. Anyone who can read the topic sees approval metadata, so use an access-controlled topic or a long random name.

url.description: Base URL of the ntfy server, for example https://ntfy.sh. Empty disables the ntfy notifier.

plugins.description: Notifier plugins by name (docs/plugins.md): `command` (absolute path of the plugin binary, owned by root or scrim's user and writable by no one else), `args`, `env` (the plugin's environment; never a credential), `options` (the plugin's own settings, validated by the plugin), `sha256` (pins the binary), `timeout` (per delivery, default 10s), `start-timeout` (default 5s), and the credential fields `token`, `password`, `secret` and `credentials` (references, resolved at every start and sent only to the plugin).

enabled.description: Print each approval request with its scrim approve and scrim deny commands to the control plane's terminal.

hold.description: Longest time one submit or poll request is held open by the receiver (sent as X-Nono-Timeout-Secs, capped by the approval's remaining time).

poll-interval.description: Pause between polls when the receiver answers pending without holding.

secret.description: Reference to the shared secret (at least 32 bytes) that signs webhook requests with HMAC-SHA256. Empty sends unsigned requests.

url.description: Approval service URL for the webhook notifier (nono approval webhook v1 compatible). https, or http to a loopback host. Empty disables it.

inject.description: Built-in rule `builtin.inject-bound` for injecting a credential toward a host it is bound to, for an identified agent: allow, ask, or off (injection is then decided by your rules and policy.default). Deny rules in the rules file still win.

default.description: Decision applied when no rule matches. Anything other than deny is reported as a weakened protection.

deny-all.description: Break-glass: deny every injection, grant and approval while redaction continues. While set in configuration it cannot be released from the CLI.

deny-all-refresh.description: How often each replica re-reads the deny-all state from the state backend; the bound on how long a change on one replica takes to reach the others when no event announces it (events.backend).

rules-file.description: Path of the policy rules file (YAML or JSON with default and rules). Empty means no rules: every request gets policy.default.

profile.description: Built-in preset of defaults for a deployment shape: `local` for a laptop or VM, `k8s` for Kubernetes, `ci` for throwaway runs. Any value a profile sets can be overridden.

access-key-id.description: Store reference to the AWS access key id.

api-key.description: Store reference to the provider API key.

client-secret.description: Store reference to the Entra ID client secret.

metadata-server.description: Take Google access tokens from the metadata server (workload identity).

secret-access-key.description: Store reference to the AWS secret access key.

service-account.description: Store reference to a Google service account key (the JSON key file).

session-token.description: Store reference to the AWS session token.

token-url.description: Token endpoint replacing the default (Google, Entra ID, or the metadata server).

providers.description: Cloud provider routes by name, each served at `/<name>` on the LLM base URL and for its provider host through the forward proxy. `kind` is `bedrock` (Amazon Bedrock runtime), `bedrock-mantle`, `anthropic-aws` (Claude Platform on AWS), `foundry` (Microsoft Foundry) or `vertex` (Google Vertex AI). `region` (AWS kinds, and the Vertex location) or `resource` (foundry) selects the endpoint, `upstream` overrides it. scrim authenticates every request itself after redaction and drops what the agent sent: `access-key-id`, `secret-access-key` and optional `session-token` sign with AWS SigV4 (AWS kinds); `api-key` sends a key (Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS as a bearer token, Foundry as `api-key`); `service-account` (a JSON key file) or `metadata-server: true` mints Google access tokens (vertex); `tenant-id`, `client-id` and `client-secret` mint Entra ID tokens (foundry). `token-url` overrides the token endpoint. Credential fields are store references, never values. Provider routes are never chained.

dir.description: Capture mode: write every provider request exactly as it left, and the response as received, to this directory (mode 0700; refused if group or others can access it). Empty disables capture. `scrim proxy --capture=DIR` sets it.

retention.description: Captured files older than this are deleted.

on-unavailable.description: When the chained upstream cannot be reached: fail refuses the request, direct sends the already redacted request to the provider and audits the skip.

url.description: Base URL of a chained upstream (for example a context compression proxy) that receives every redacted provider request in place of the provider. Empty means no chain.

forward-listen.description: TCP address of the forward proxy for agents with HTTPS_PROXY set (scrim run sets it): provider hosts go to the LLM proxy, every other host to the tool proxy with credential injection. Empty disables it; keep it on loopback.

listen.description: TCP address of the LLM proxy base URL (agents use http://<address>/anthropic and http://<address>/openai/v1). Empty disables it; keep it on loopback.

sni-listen.description: TCP address of the SNI listener for DNS override mode: provider names resolve to its address (scrim install --dns writes /etc/hosts entries and sets 127.0.83.1:443), it serves certificates for them from the scrim CA and routes by TLS server name. Connections made by address bypass it. Empty disables it.

socket.description: Unix socket path for the LLM proxy base URL, for agents that can connect to one. Empty disables it.

transparent-listen.description: TCP addresses of the transparent listener (Linux): connections redirected to it by nftables are routed by TLS server name or Host header, provider hosts to the LLM proxy, bound tool hosts to the tool proxy. scrim install --transparent sets 127.0.0.1:9793 and [::1]:9793 (9792 is metrics.listen). Empty disables it.

transparent-unrouted.description: What the transparent and SNI listeners do with a host that is neither a provider host nor bound to a credential or capture rule: pass relays the connection untouched to that host name (never to the address the client dialled), block closes it. TLS without a server name is always closed.

anthropic.description: Base URL Anthropic Messages requests are forwarded to after redaction.

chatgpt.description: Base URL requests to chatgpt.com (Codex signed in with ChatGPT, through the forward proxy) are forwarded to after redaction.

chatgpt-ab.description: Base URL requests to ab.chatgpt.com (Codex signed in with ChatGPT, through the forward proxy) are forwarded to after redaction. Its API shape is not documented, so every request body is redacted as generic JSON.

gemini.description: Base URL Gemini API (generateContent, streamGenerateContent, countTokens) requests are forwarded to after redaction.

openai.description: Base URL OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses requests are forwarded to after redaction.

burst.description: How many agent API calls (local API and MCP tools) one agent may make at once before ratelimit.agent-api.rate applies.

rate.description: How many agent API calls (local API and MCP tools) one agent may make per ratelimit.agent-api.interval, after its burst; 0 turns the limit off.

burst.description: How many approval requests (tool calls and proxied requests held for a human) one agent may make at once before ratelimit.approvals.rate applies.

rate.description: How many approval requests (tool calls and proxied requests held for a human) one agent may make per ratelimit.approvals.interval, after its burst; 0 turns the limit off.

burst.description: How many secret_ask_human asks one agent may make at once before ratelimit.asks.rate applies.

rate.description: How many secret_ask_human asks one agent may make per ratelimit.asks.interval, after its burst; 0 turns the limit off.

backend.description: Where per-agent rate limits are counted. local counts in each replica's memory, so with several replicas an agent can get up to that many times each limit (approximate); valkey counts in Valkey (valkey.*), one exact limit shared by every replica. When the backend cannot answer, the request is refused.

prefix.description: Prefix of the Valkey keys ratelimit.backend valkey keeps its counters in. Replicas of one deployment share it; two deployments on one Valkey need different prefixes.

allow-empty-targets.description: Start even when a store's redact target matches no secret on the first load. Off, such a target stops start-up with an error naming it, since it usually means a misspelt name or pattern and redaction would protect nothing. On, the store starts and status reports the target as degraded with 0 values.

min-value-length.description: Shortest value matched in free text; shorter values are matched only in exact and encoded forms.

placeholder-key-dir.description: Directory of the generated placeholder key, used when redaction.placeholder-keys is empty. Empty means $XDG_STATE_HOME/scrim/keys (~/.local/state/scrim/keys).

placeholder-keys.description: Placeholder keys by name, each with `version` (1 to 255) and `key` (a reference to at least 16 bytes). The highest version is current; lower ones keep resolving placeholders made before a rotation. Every replica sharing conversations needs the same keys. Empty means a key generated once and kept in redaction.placeholder-key-dir.

allow-reveal-credentials.description: Glob patterns over store references of credentials that scrim reveal may resolve locally. Empty means reveal never resolves a credential. Restore into responses never resolves credentials, whatever this holds.

allow-shell-data-commands.description: Commands a shell-role restore may pass display values to, beyond the built-in list of commands that run no code. A listed command that interprets an argument as code turns a restored value into code.

builtin-tools.description: Use the built-in table of agent tool roles (Claude Code, Codex). When false only restore.tools have roles and every other tool is unknown, which restores nothing.

display-mode.description: What the agent displays for display-class values: values resolves them in assistant text, placeholders keeps placeholders (for example while screen sharing). Tool arguments follow the tool roles either way; credentials are never restored.

tools.description: Tool aliases by name: `role` (none, read, search, shell, edit, write, network), optional `name` (the tool name exactly as the model calls it, default the instance name), `command-field` for shell, `old-fields` and `new-fields` for edit. An alias overrides the built-in table.

allow-unredacted-start.description: Start the agent anyway when scrim cannot start, its data plane is not ready or no session can be minted. The agent then reaches providers directly and unredacted; scrim run prints a warning.

fs-view.description: Session filesystem view for credential files at fixed home paths: auto (a user and mount namespace where the host allows it, the home mirror elsewhere), namespace (refuse to start the agent without one), home (HOME points at a mirror of the home directory without the real credential files) or off. See docs/run.md.

fs-view-hide.description: Home-relative paths or glob patterns hidden by the session filesystem view in addition to the fixed paths of the applied tool profiles; a leading ! takes matches out again.

mcp.description: Register scrim mcp with the agent for this session (Claude Code --mcp-config, Codex -c mcp_servers.scrim). Nothing is written to the agent's own configuration.

placeholder-env.description: Export each declared catalog placeholder that resolves for the session as an environment variable of the same name holding the placeholder, for example SCRIM_ACME_KEY=SCRIM_ACME_KEY.

profiles.description: Tool profiles scrim run applies: profile names, `auto` for every profile at least one catalog entry fills (an entry naming the profile in its tools list), or `none`. Profiles a selected one requires are added. See docs/cli-tools.md.

scan-interval.description: How often scrim run rescans the project files while the agent runs and registers changed values; 0 scans once at start.

scan-project.description: Scan the agent's working directory for secret values in project files (.env*, *.tfvars, application config, compose files, .npmrc) and redact them from the session's first request. scrim run refuses to start the agent when they cannot be registered.

ssh-agent.description: Point SSH_AUTH_SOCK at scrim's ssh-agent for the session: ssh and git over ssh sign with the catalog's ssh_key entries, decided and audited by scrim, and an inherited agent with your own keys is not reachable through it.

max-ttl.description: Longest lifetime a session token can be minted with.

ttl.description: Default lifetime of a session token minted by scrim run. The token is revoked earlier when scrim run exits.

known-hosts.description: known_hosts files (OpenSSH format) that name the hosts scrim's ssh-agent signs logins for: a login whose session binding verifies a host key listed here sees that line's first plain host name as dest.host. Use files the agent cannot write; hashed and wildcard entries are not used.

backend.description: State backend for approvals, grants, sessions and audit metadata. The local profile uses sqlite ($XDG_STATE_HOME/scrim/state.db); ci and k8s use memory, which writes nothing to disk (set postgres for shared state).

connect-timeout.description: How long start-up waits for PostgreSQL to answer before failing.

dsn.description: Reference to the PostgreSQL connection string (postgres://user:pass@host/db?sslmode=verify-full), for example env:SCRIM_PG_DSN or file:/run/secrets/scrim-dsn. It holds a password, so it is a reference.

max-conns.description: Maximum connections in the PostgreSQL pool.

allow-network-filesystem.description: Allows the SQLite state file on a network or shared filesystem (NFS, SMB, sshfs), where file locking is unreliable and the database can be corrupted. Use the postgres backend instead.

labels.description: Derived policy labels by name: a source label name to copy, or {from, regex, value}.

stores.description: Secret store instances by name. The name is the instance's reference scheme (`bao://...` for an instance named bao); `kind` picks the adapter, `aliases` adds schemes, `redact` lists references and prefixes loaded into the redaction set, `refresh.*` tunes refresh and outage handling, `labels` derives policy labels from the store's own labels (docs/policy.md, "Labels from stores"), and every other field is the adapter's own. See docs/stores.

tool-profiles.description: Tool profiles by name: description, tools, requires, credentials (name, hosts, inject, required), params, env, unset, dirs, files (path, content), paths (home, generated), test (command, expect), notes. A name that matches a built-in profile overrides the fields it sets (params are merged key by key). Templates hold placeholders only, never values. See docs/cli-tools.md.

cert-file.description: PEM certificate of an operator-supplied interception CA, used together with tool-proxy.ca.key. An operator-supplied CA is never rotated by scrim; a warning is logged once it is within tool-proxy.ca.rotate-before of expiry.

dir.description: Directory of the generated interception CA (certificates, private keys, rotation state, trust manifest). Empty means $XDG_STATE_HOME/scrim/ca (~/.local/state/scrim/ca). Created with mode 0700.

key.description: Reference to the PKCS#8 PEM private key of the operator-supplied CA in tool-proxy.ca.cert-file (env:, file:, cred: or a store reference). Empty means scrim generates and rotates its own CA.

overlap.description: After a rotation, how long the previous CA stays trusted through a cross certificate and in the trust bundle. Capped at the previous certificate's expiry.

rotate-before.description: A generated CA is rotated when less than this much of its validity remains. For an operator-supplied CA it is how early the expiry warning starts.

validity.description: Validity of each generated CA certificate.

capture-rules.description: Response capture rules by name: `hosts`, optional `methods`, `path` glob and `status` codes select the response; exactly one of `json-pointer` and `header` selects the field; `store-ref` is the store reference the value is written to. The agent receives the reference's placeholder instead.

listen.description: TCP address of the HTTPS tool proxy (credential injection and response redaction) for tools pointed at it directly. Empty disables it.

approval-timeout.description: How long a pending approval waits for a decision before it expires as denied.

grant-default-ttl.description: Duration of a grant when secret_request names none.

grant-max-ttl.description: Longest grant secret_request can produce. Longer requests are capped and the result says so.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP collector URL for traces, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318. Empty disables export; incoming W3C trace context is still propagated.

sample-ratio.description: Fraction of new root traces sampled, 0 to 1. A sampled incoming parent is always followed.

addresses.description: Valkey (or Redis-compatible) servers as host:port, used by events.backend valkey and ratelimit.backend valkey. Several addresses of one cluster are seeds; the client discovers the rest.

password.description: Reference to the Valkey password (env:, file:, cred: or a store reference); empty for none.

timeout.description: Dial timeout and the bound on one Valkey round trip; a connection that does not answer a ping within it is considered dead and replaced.

tls.description: Connect to Valkey over TLS, verifying the server against the system roots or valkey.tls-ca-file.

tls-ca-file.description: PEM file of the certificate authorities that sign the Valkey server certificate; empty uses the system roots.

username.description: Valkey ACL user; empty uses the default user.
